blocks.text: 今年的一切都关乎势头。过去 12 个月，开发者向 GitHub 推送代码变更 179 亿次，超过 2024 年和 2025 年的总和。所有仓库类型（公共和私有）的提交次数增长更快，达到 343 亿次，是两年前的三倍多。同期合并的拉取请求增长了两倍多，达到 13 亿个，平均每天 350 万个。

blocks.text: 我们的遥测数据显示，活动从 1 月起稳步攀升，随后在 6 月前后激增，仿佛各地的开发者同时看到了新的可能性。大约就在那时，一系列行业范围的转变同时发生：更强大的底层模型、围绕它们构建的框架与工具，以及运行在两者之上的智能体。智能体从单会话工具转变为持久化工具，能够跨天跟踪进度并编排其他专用智能体。同样重要的是，智能体开始大量使用云端，既在本地机器上执行工作，也能远程执行。

blocks.text: Our telemetry shows activity climbing steadily from January, then surging around June, as if developers everywhere saw new possibilities at once. blocks.text: One year in, growth is strong against last year’s projection, and projecting the next five years is getting harder. We ran more than 40 forecasting models forward to 2031, time-series and regression models built on historical sign-up and usage data, each assuming a different pace of growth. About half call for “extreme” growth, with developer counts on GitHub more than tripling by 2031. Just under half call for “substantial” growth, doubling to tripling. Only three models expect anything close to modest, under 2x growth.

blocks.text: Behind these sector shifts are people who know their fields, now using AI coding agents to build. For example, in manufacturing, a small team built a way to turn a photo of your tools into a custom-fit, 3D-printable drawer organizer. A research lab in health care made it easier for scientists to analyze huge digital scans of tissue samples, the kind pathologists study to understand disease. In Copenhagen, a university lab built a pipeline that classifies video of chickens at play, from frolicking to worm chasing. A University of Waikato energy center built a toolkit that helps industrial plants find heat they can reuse, and Bulgaria’s digital ministry open-sourced a portal where anyone can trace who won a public contract and for how much. For writers, a novelist built a free app that makes a manuscript look like a book as you type. In field after field, the people closest to the problem are building the solution, with agents helping along the way.

blocks.text: Review is where developers shape what comes back, and more tooling is being built for it. Stacked pull requests, which split related work into smaller changes that are easier to review in sequence, launched as a preview on July 30, and more than 264,000 developers had used them by September. Usage of AI-assisted code review and GitHub Advanced Security both grew more than 90% year over year. The platform also helps secure that work: push protection, which screens for exposed secrets such as API keys and passwords, ran 5.8 billion scans this year, nearly four times 2025’s pace. Developers are investing in how they review code.

blocks.text: Last year, we reported that TypeScript had overtaken Python and JavaScript to become the most used language on GitHub by contributors. That order held in 2026, with TypeScript first, Python second, and JavaScript third. The pace picked up. Rust grew fastest by percentage among the top languages, doubling in the past year.

blocks.text: This year, we split the fastest-growing and most-engaged projects on GitHub into two groups: community and independent repositories, and single-vendor or product-led ones. Community and independent projects are foundation-governed, broadly maintained, or led by an individual without a clear commercial sponsor. Single-vendor and product-led projects are open source or source-available and often take substantial community contributions, but strategic control sits with one company.

The growth list also includes places built to welcome newcomers, like first-contributions and is-a-dev/register, where many developers make their first pull request.

And someone still has to decide whether it works, whether it belongs, and whether it’s good.

A push sends one or more commits to GitHub. Contributions count each push once, so commit totals can exceed contribution totals. Actions are counted in jobs, not minutes. Open-source contributions (2.5 billion) are public.
Contributor and contribution counts exclude spam-flagged accounts, staff, and bots where identifiable.

Developers are mapped to countries by self-reported location, with a 100-developer publication threshold. Octoverse 2025 published 2030 totals, not annual targets. Progress is net developers added from September 2025 to September 2026 as a share of the distance from each country’s published 2025 count to its 2030 projection.

Contributors are distinct accounts each month that took part through pushes, pull requests, issues, reviews, or comments, attributed to each repository’s primary language (Linguist). An account can count in several languages. This follows the Octoverse 2025 method. Forecasts cover the top 10 languages by average monthly participation and project to September 2027 (mean shown).
compares growth in monthly participating accounts between September 2025 and September 2026 with the share of merged pull requests with detected AI involvement. Bubble size reflects community size.
Top countries by pushes to public repositories, adjusted by profile location.

Pushes from each country were summed across the Octoverse year. To adjust for biases caused by VPN usage, LLM classification was used to extract the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code from the profiles of GitHub users who contributed pushes during this period, which were then used to construct ratios of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes based on profile location vs. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes based on IP address. These ratios were then used to weight the pushes from each country.

Public repositories created 2022 to 2026 were sorted into NAICS sectors by a fine-tuned multilingual embedding model using name, description, topics, and README, from random samples per year. AI mentions and agent-opened pull requests (detectable agents only) were flagged as separate signals. Sector and AI-mention shares can be related because both read the same text. Shares are estimates.

Repositories are classed as community or single-vendor by who holds strategic control. “Fastest-growing” ranks by the absolute year-over-year increase in distinct contributing accounts. “Most engaged” blends a repository’s rankings for stars, forks, and distinct pull request and issue creators. Forked repositories are excluded from both lists.

Figures cover GitHub Copilot and count developer-selected requests only. They exclude auto model selection, staff usage, duplicate monitoring requests, background utility models, and requests made with a developer’s own API key. Each model needs at least 1,000 weekly active users to count. Models are grouped by what they are built for, with examples listed alphabetically by provider:
Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT 6 Luna.
Figures describe observed use, not model quality. Trend observations use weekly data from July 14 to October 13, 2026.
is the share of all qualifying requests per model group in a 7-day period ending October 13, 2026.

Counts public repositories created each year whose name, description, topics, or README mention interoperability or reverse engineering, or related terms, such as clean room implementation, drop-in replacement, or protocol re-implementation.

We ran 43 time-series and regression models on historical GitHub data, sign-ups, product usage, and market sizing, projecting developers on GitHub to September 2031 relative to September 2026. Outcomes group as 3x or more (21 models), 2x to under 3x (19), and under 2x (3). Octoverse 2025 used five models. No forecast is perfectly accurate.
